:::{#def-kolmogorov-complexity}
#### Kolmogorov complexity

Fix a universal computer $U$:
a Turing machine, or an interpreter for a programming language,
that reads a program $p$, a finite string of binary digits,
and either runs forever or halts and outputs a binary string $U(p)$.
Assume no program on which $U$ halts is a proper prefix of another,
as happens when $U$ reads its program one digit at a time
and must itself decide where the program ends.

The **Kolmogorov complexity** of a binary string $x$ is
the length of a shortest program that outputs $x$:

$$K(x) \eqdef \min \{ \abs{p} : U(p) = x \},$$

where $\abs{p}$ is the number of digits in $p$.
The **conditional Kolmogorov complexity** $K(x \mid n)$ is defined the same way,
except that $U$ is also given the integer $n$ as an input.
This is the definition of @cover2006elements [section 14.2].

:::
